validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification, and spec (except StartYear1 -- see the separate concern entry) all confirm. The gem.wiki page's only cited support (wiki_citations.json) is the generic PNGRB data-bank landing page (pngrb.gov.in/eng-web/data-bank.html#ngpl-1 / #bm6), an aggregate index that does not itself name this pipeline -- by the task's own criterion that would be a weak/generic citation, so I went to the regulator's actual line-wise table instead. PNGRB's monthly 'Natural Gas Pipelines Network in India' MIS report, edition '20260531' (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, curl-confirmed HTTP 200, 15pp, fetched and read with pdftotext -layout), lists under 'PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE', row 2: 'Bhatinda - Gurdaspur | GIGL | Authorisation 07.07.2011 | Authorised Length 261 km | Authorised Capacity 42.4 MMSCMD | Determined Capacity 42.4 | Gas Supplied 0.1 | Utilisation 0.3% | Operating Length 101 km | Construction Length 160 km | ... | Target Dec-24 | States: PB'. That corroborates: Status=operating (the 101 km IS the in-service portion of a partially-commissioned asset -- GEM's separate P3913 'Phase II' correctly carries the remaining under-construction length as its own construction-status row, the documented granularity pattern for Indian gas pipelines, not a duplicate); PipelineType=transmission (listed under 'COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE', an interstate transmission classification, correct); Fuel=Gas (NGPL = Natural Gas Pipeline, correct); Capacity=42.42 MMSCMD (PNGRB's rounded 42.4 matches to the precision the MIS table prints, and GEM's more precise 42.42 is corroborated exactly by a second, older PNGRB document -- see below); LengthKnown=102.00 km (PNGRB's current Operating Length is 101 km, i.e. matches to within 1 km -- plausibly a small subsequent addition/rounding, immaterial); StartLocation=Bhatinda / EndLocation=Gurdaspur / StartState=EndState=Punjab (PNGRB's States column reads 'PB' only, consistent with an intra-Punjab segment). GIGL (GSPL India Gasnet Limited, a JV of GSPL/IOCL/BPCL/HPCL) building a Mehsana-Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar gas corridor is independently corroborated by an Economic Times article in the working cache (et_article.html) describing the JV and its phased construction, though that piece does not give this specific sub-segment's length/capacity. Separately, a cached PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 (ar1920.txt, Part 3 NGPL section, table 'Partially Commissioned NGPL: Commissioned (As on 30 June 2020)') lists unique ID 5.02.NGPL 'Bhatinda - Jammu - Srinagar', Entity GSPL India Gasnet Limited, Authorised Length 725 km, Authorised Capacity 42.42 MMSCMD (exact match to GEM's 42.42), Authorisation Date 07.07.2011, Commissioned Length/ready-for-gas-in 102 km (exact match to GEM's 102.00), target completion 24.02.2022, States Punjab/J&K -- confirming the same 102 km figure from a second PNGRB vintage, six years apart, with byte-for-byte matching capacity. I could not re-locate/re-verify a live URL for that 2019-20 Annual Report within this session's search budget (WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task and pngrb.gov.in has no discoverable /annual-report path from the current site or common guesses; Wayback CDX was rate-limited), so I am NOT proposing it as a citable ref (no fabricated URLs per standing rule 2) -- only the current, live-verified MIS PDF is proposed below. Both readings are the same origin (PNGRB, the sector regulator) rather than two independent organizations, so I am rating this tier=medium, independent=false, not high, despite the strong internal consistency -- a second, non-regulator corroboration (a GIGL/GSPL/GSPL-Transmission investor disclosure or credit-rating report naming this specific segment) was not found in the time available and should be sought before upgrading the tier. url_verifier.py returns a false positive-negative on the MIS PDF (HTTP 200 but 'missing expected' for every token tried, including 'Bhatinda', 'PNGRB', 'Natural Gas') -- this matches the documented large-PDF false-negative in this run's India scope guidance; the content was confirmed locally via curl + pdftotext, not via the verifier's keyword match.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=2023 for this row. That conflicts with the PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 table described above ('Partially Commissioned NGPL: Commissioned (As on 30 June 2020)'), which lists unique ID 5.02.NGPL 'Bhatinda - Jammu - Srinagar' (GSPL India Gasnet Limited) with Commissioned Length/ready-for-gas-in = 102 km -- the exact figure GEM carries for this row -- under an 'As on 30 June, 2020' snapshot table. If that 102 km was already commissioned/ready-for-gas-in as of 30 June 2020, GEM's StartYear1 of 2023 is off by roughly three years. This is a material disagreement per the standing corroboration rule, so I am flagging it rather than silently passing the existing value. I am NOT proposing a replacement value/ref: the only document with a precise date is one I found in this run's shared scratchpad cache but could not re-verify at a live URL within the exhausted web-search budget (no pngrb.gov.in path for an 'annual report 2019-20' PDF was discoverable by direct guesses, and Wayback CDX search was rate-limited -- 429 -- when tried). A future pass should locate a live/archived copy of the PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 (Part 3, Natural Gas Pipelines) or a GIGL/GSPL investor disclosure naming this segment's actual commissioning date, then correct StartYear1 through Update with a verified citation. Authorisation date (07.07.2011) is explicitly NOT a candidate replacement per this country's own guidance -- it precedes physical construction by years.

fills.researcher_notes: PNGRB NGPL MIS report (20260531 edition), 'Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Pipeline' table: Bhatinda-Gurdaspur (GIGL) shows Operating Length 101 km against Authorised Length 261 km -- the operating portion is real, in-service pipe, matching GEM's operating status for this Phase I row. url_verifier gives a false-negative keyword miss on this large PDF (documented issue); confirmed locally via curl 200 + pdftotext -layout.
Listed as a Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) in PNGRB's register; fuel = gas is inherent to the report's scope.
Listed under PNGRB's 'COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' section -- an interstate common-carrier gas transmission pipeline, confirming the transmission classification (not a gathering/feeder/dedicated line).

PNGRB's current MIS report gives Authorised/Determined Capacity 42.4 MMSCMD for Bhatinda-Gurdaspur (rounds to GEM's 42.42); a second, older PNGRB document (Annual Report 2019-20, not independently citable at a live URL in this pass -- see validity notes) gives the same figure to two decimal places, 42.42, for the same GIGL segment.

PNGRB's current MIS report gives Operating Length 101 km for Bhatinda-Gurdaspur (within 1 km of GEM's 102.00, immaterial); the 2019-20 PNGRB Annual Report gives 102 km exactly for the same commissioned portion (not independently citable at a live URL in this pass -- see validity notes).
Pipeline is named 'Bhatinda - Gurdaspur' in PNGRB's register with States Passing Through = 'PB' (Punjab) only, consistent with both endpoints being within Punjab.

summary: P5533 (Bhatinda-Gurdaspur, Phase I, operating, 102km/42.42 MMSCMD) is a real, correctly-classified GIGL common-carrier transmission segment -- confirmed against PNGRB's current NGPL MIS register (101km operating / 261km authorised) and, on capacity/length exactly, a second PNGRB vintage (AR2019-20); 6 fields (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Length/Location) filled with that PNGRB ref (tier=medium, single-origin regulator). One real concern: StartYear1=2023 looks wrong -- PNGRB's own 2019-20 Annual Report shows this same 102km segment already commissioned by 30 June 2020, ~3 years earlier -- flagged as a spec concern, left UNRESOLVED (no live-verifiable date source found this pass, so no replacement value proposed). Not a duplicate of P3913 (Phase II, construction) or P5413 (Gurdaspur-Jammu) -- that split matches the documented Indian operating/under-construction granularity pattern -- though the family's total length looks off (GEM Phase I+II = 392km vs PNGRB's 261km authorised for Bhatinda-Gurdaspur), worth a look when P3913 itself is swept.
